title: Australia declared war on birds. And lost.

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: In 1932, Australia sent machine guns after 20,000 emus.
beats.visual: Sketch emu flock stampeding across a wheat field toward camera, dust trails

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: Farmers near Campion, Western Australia, called in the army's Major Meredith.
beats.visual: Sketch map of Western Australia; pin drops on Campion between Perth and Kalgoorlie

beats.speaker: q
beats.visual: Ava icon; emu peeking over a fence post

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: The emus were wrecking wheat. The army brought two Lewis guns, 10,000 rounds. But there was a problem.
beats.visual: PD photo 'Lewis Gun during Emu War' slides in; bullet counter ticks to 10,000

beats.speaker: q
beats.visual: Ava icon; one emu stares into the lens

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: Scatter. Flocks split up. A gun jammed. A gun on a truck couldn't keep up.
beats.visual: Three fast panels: flock bursts into small dots; jammed gun with smoke puff; truck bouncing behind running emus

beats.speaker: q
beats.visual: Ava icon; scoreboard ARMY vs EMUS

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: The emus. Meredith said they faced machine guns with the invulnerability of tanks. By December, the soldiers were recalled.
beats.visual: PD photo 'Emus coming to drink'; quote card 'the invulnerability of tanks'; army truck drives off

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: Farmers went back to bounties. One MP joked about medals.
beats.visual: Bounty coins stack up; cartoon medal with an emu on it

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: Australia fought birds, and lost. Follow History Sketches for one wild true story every day.
beats.visual: Emu standing on the empty gun position; History Sketches corner logo

description: In 1932 the Australian army took two machine guns to Western Australia's wheat belt to stop around 20,000 emus. The birds scattered, a gun jammed, and the soldiers were recalled. Narration: synthetic voices. Facts checked against two sources. #history #shorts #australia #emuwar
